items.basis: Returns are remelted and valued at charge cost C, so C = sum(fresh share x price)/(fresh share). Mix A (KTU 'basic' ductile charge: 60% pig iron, 10% mild steel, 26% returns, ~4% FeSi+carburiser; the 4% treated as at C): (0.60x47.05 + 0.10x39.8)/0.70 = 46.01. Mix B (steel-rich, >50% steel scrap - per the Estonian study gives finer nodules; KTU notes steel scrap is cheaper but limits nucleation): 20% pig + 50% low-Mn CR busheling + 30% returns: (0.20x47.05 + 0.50x39.8)/0.70 = 41.87. Range 41.87-46.01.
items.notes: EXCLUDES FeSiMg treatment, inoculant, carburiser, Cu/Mn alloying, melt loss and melt power (not priced; the tool charges melt energy/loss separately). Example: FeSi at 1% adds 0.01x(95.1-46.01) = 0.49. Pig iron 47.05 is a Ludhiana print (north); IIF Mar 2026 Ahmedabad 44.0 would lower Mix A by 2.61. Other charge-practice sources: https://journals.pan.pl//Content/127177/PDF/AFE%202_2023_10_final%20version.pdf (pig iron often ~half the charge), https://kirj.ee/wp-content/plugins/kirj/pub/eng-1-2004-10-17_20230304230227.pdf (>50% steel scrap), IIF guidance https://www.foundryinfo-india.org/images/pdf/3B1.pdf . No Indian published cost per kg of liquid iron found.

items.basis: Mix (CostVision engineering assumption - NO source found for an Indian grey-iron charge mix): 40% steel scrap (low-Mn CR busheling 39.8) + 20% foundry pig iron (47.05) + 40% returns valued at C: (0.40x39.8 + 0.20x47.05)/0.60 = 42.22; + FeSi70 0.5% -> +0.005x(95.1-42.22) and FeMn70 0.3% -> +0.003x(79.2-42.22) = 42.6.
items.notes: Excludes carburiser (steel-rich grey charges need ~1-2% C pick-up; carburiser price not found), inoculant, melt loss, power. CI borings price not found (would lower it).

notes: WebFetch and curl were blocked (DNS failure / proxy 403) for every price site; ALL figures were read from web-search result extracts. Each source URL is the page the extract quoted; re-verify before a refresh is committed.

GST: JPC/Ministry retail prices are GST-inclusive and were divided by 1.18. BigMint/SMM trade assessments are quoted excluding 18% GST where the extract says so; where the extract is silent it is stated in the item.

Location: no source quotes Pune/Chennai/Bengaluru/Delhi NCR separately for most items. Flat anchors use JPC's 4-metro average (Kolkata/Delhi/Mumbai/Chennai) plus Delhi and Chennai CEIC prints; long, alloy and foundry inputs are Mumbai, Raipur, Ludhiana, Durgapur, Jajpur, Guwahati prints (freight to the clusters NOT added).
Validation: JPC Mumbai retail ex-GST in May 2026 (HR 58,466; CR 66,203) matched BigMint trade (HR 58,500; CR 65,200) within INR 1,000/t, so JPC ex-GST retail is used as the trade-level anchor.

Pricing rule for the 134 grades: grade = anchor + extra. Only CR-over-HR, GP-over-CR and HRPO-over-HR extras are sourced. Automotive (IF, HSLA, DP/TRIP/CP/MS, 22MnB5/Usibor, BH, coatings), alloy-bar, bearing, free-cutting, spring, stainless-family and electrical-grade extras were NOT found.

Charge costs exclude melt loss and melt power (the engine adds both) and every addition whose price was not found (FeSiMg, inoculant, carburiser, Cu, FeMo). Returns are valued at charge cost, so C = sum(fresh share x price) / fresh share.
